text: Alright, today we're configuring this L298N dual H-bridge motor driver for our DC motor setup. First, I'm connecting the 12-volt power supply to the VCC terminal here - you can see the red wire going in. The input voltage range for this driver is 5 to 35 volts, so our 12 volts is well within spec. Now, while holding the driver steady, I'm using this Phillips head screwdriver to tighten the terminal screw - about three quarter turns should do it. Next, I need to set the current limit using this multimeter. I'm placing the red probe on the VREF pin - that's this small test point right here - and the black probe goes to ground. Currently reading 0.8 volts, which translates to about 1.6 amps of current limit using the formula VREF divided by 0.5. For our 2-amp motor, I need to increase this to 1 volt. Using this small flathead screwdriver, I'm turning the potentiometer clockwise - there we go, now reading exactly 1.0 volts. That gives us our 2-amp current limit. After that, I'm connecting the motor leads to outputs A and B - the blue and yellow wires from our gearmotor go into the screw terminals. Finally, the enable pins EN1 and EN2 get connected to our Arduino's PWM outputs - pins 9 and 10 respectively. The driver is now pulling about 50 milliamps at idle, which is normal. Remember, always connect power before signal lines to prevent latch-up conditions.
